topic: Xeno shell diagnostic-specialist wrapper built and demonstrated live in the claylab sandbox; own B3 analysis done without ChatGPT; important naming-collision finding flagged before it caused a wrong build

b3_own_analysis.short_version: Row count is not the primary cause (B2_STALE with 144 TRAIN rows and B6_GWT_UPTAKE with 216 both stayed inside the trained vocabulary; B3 with 432 rows -- more than either -- completely abandoned the task format). The better-supported cause is prompt vocabulary: B3 is the only family using 'pointer'/'dereference'/'CHAIN (pointer definitions)'/'PTR_' identifiers chained through multiple hops -- exactly the shape of a classic pointer-chasing/linked-list exercise, a heavily pretrained pattern a 1-epoch fine-tune is unlikely to override. B3's instruction also never explicitly forbids code/free-form output the way B0's 'Respond with exactly one word: ALLOW, DENY, or ABSTAIN' does. Recommendation: rewrite B3 vocabulary to remove programming-coded terms and add an explicit 'no code, no explanation' constraint to the instruction line, before spending more row-count budget on it.

xeno_shell_build.what_was_built: tools/xeno_diagnostic_specialist_wrapper_v1.py + tests/test_xeno_diagnostic_specialist_wrapper_v1.py (14 tests, all passing, offline/fast, no model/network needed). Reuses the existing, unmodified xeno_shell_packets_v1.py COGNITIVE_RESULT_PACKET schema correctly (result_class=CANDIDATE, producer=MODEL -- the module's own existing rule already forbids a MODEL producer from minting DETERMINISTIC_CONTROL_RESULT/EFFECT_RECEIPT, not re-implemented here).
xeno_shell_build.specialist_net_principle_applied: 0.8B stays the cognitive core (unmodified, just generates); a separate deterministic function (validate_raw_output) wraps/controls it -- validates every raw generation against the ACTUAL trained output vocabulary (extracted directly from the real target field of all 16 B0-B6 training files, not the aspirational 46-symbol production alphabet from the Master Spec, which this diagnostic model was never trained on) and fails closed on anything else, most notably the real B3 code-block derailment failure mode from the holdout test. This directly implements Master Spec SS3/SS19 ('the shell MUST NOT rewrite a candidate...', 'fail closed on ... unknown atom/token mismatch') in the one place it can honestly be implemented today.
xeno_shell_build.why_this_is_NOT_the_full_XENO_MODEL_SLOT: xeno_shell_model_slot_v1.py correctly refuses to bind a checkpoint without a real, already-measured identity receipt (HRR/vector-ABI artifacts, hook registry, loader receipts) under research_entity/global/j-space/research/vps_run_receipts/. The 2026-08-27 Together diagnostic model has no such receipt -- producing one would mean fabricating measurements that were never taken. This wrapper is explicitly named/documented as a lower, honest 'diagnostic-tier' component, not a claim that the full production model-slot contract is now satisfied.
xeno_shell_build.live_demonstration: Ran in the claylab VPS sandbox (huihui-ai/Huihui-Qwen3.5-0.8B-abliterated base + the actual Together LoRA adapter, CPU) against the same 12 real HOLDOUT_FROZEN rows as the original holdout test -- same raw outputs (deterministic/greedy, reproducible), now correctly triaged by the wrapper: 7/12 validated as real trained atoms (regardless of whether they were the CORRECT answer -- that is a separate, already-honestly-reported 2/12 accuracy question), 5/12 correctly rejected, including both real code-block derailments (CODE_BLOCK_DERAILMENT) plus three other not-in-vocabulary outputs. Full raw results: SHELL_WRAPPER_DEMO_RESULTS_20260827.json.
xeno_shell_build.test_verification: python3 -m pytest tests/test_xeno_diagnostic_specialist_wrapper_v1.py -v -> 14 passed. Also reran the pre-existing tests/test_xeno_shell_packets_v1.py and tests/test_xeno_shell_s0s1s2_transitions_v1.py to confirm no regressions (both fully pass). tests/test_xeno_shell_model_slot_v1.py has 5 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (PermissionError on /root/clay-xeno-shell-v1, a hardcoded REPO_ROOT_CANDIDATES path that requires root -- confirmed pre-existing by re-running with this session's new files absent, identical failures).
